chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to us, saying: Al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Khazzaz narrated to us, from Ghiyath ibn Ibrahim, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather (peace be upon them).

He said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) passed by a group of people who were lifting a stone, and he said: What is this? They said: By that, we know the most severe among us and the strongest among us. Then he (peace be upon him and his Family) said: Shall I not inform you of the most severe among you and the strongest among you? They said: Yes, O Messenger of Allah. He said: The most severe among you and the strongest among you is the one whom, if he is pleased, his satisfaction does not lead him into sin or falsehood, and if he is angered, his anger does not cause him to leave the saying of truth, and if he is able, he does not take that which is not his by right.
ai.seo_question: What is the definition of true strength and severity in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Mani al-Akhbar*, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) redefines strength (*quwwah*) as spiritual resilience and moral integrity rather than physical might, a concept central to Shia ethics regarding the balance of *hilm* (forbearance) and *ghadab* (anger). This definition aligns with the Imams' teaching that true power lies in mastering one's ego (*nafs*) to remain just in joy and truthful in wrath, reflecting the ideal character of the Ahl al-Bayt.
